proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived an explicit complete-null finite-level W1 test over atomic compact signals with unequal centered variance-bounded channels and a matching full marked-product converse giving the sharp full-class loglog(n)/log(n) order for blind and disclosed paired records. It also proved a fixed single-reading obstruction, a sharp noiseless root-n endpoint, and an ordinary-smooth upper bound of order polylog(n) times n^(-1/(12 beta+6)); its root-n obstruction does not match this upper rate, so the fastest ordinary-smooth rate and simultaneous adaptation remain open. D0.5 passed mathematical review and verified the Hermite citation but graded the package subfield below the field floor; no F stage, Lean module, or machine-checked proof was produced.
tldr: Differential endpoint channels can invalidate a latent-distribution no-effect report even in a randomized trial. The theorem makes duplicate independent readings sufficient for an exactly finite-level, computable test over all compact latent probability laws and centered arm-specific error laws with second moments at most one. Its sharp full-class Wasserstein separation order is \(\log\log n/\log n\), unchanged in the worst case when the same records disclose both channels. An identical first-reading null and alternative establish a fixed positive obstruction without duplicates. The noiseless adaptive endpoint is sharply root-n, while the fastest ordinary-smooth rate remains open within an explicit honest bracket.
gap: Existing latent-homogeneity tests already permit different group channels. The missing comparison is exact finite-sample complete-null validity and a sharp uniform Wasserstein testing boundary for atomic bounded signals under asymmetric variance-only error laws.
fill: The local transform certificate, finite quadrature attainer, compact-law modulus, and normalized full marked-product converse jointly determine the blind and disclosed worst-class radii. The first-reading collision delimits uniform no-effect testing impossibility.
